extracted.intended_audience: aspiring television/film writers, production crew, and general readers interested in TV/film production roles
extracted.subtask_description: Responsibilities and expectations for the story editor position in motion picture and television production, describing duties in both live-action and American animation contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding new script/breakdown writers
rubrics_metrics.description: The story editor has many responsibilities, including finding new script/breakdown writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Live-action responsibility: sourcing writing talent is an explicit part of the role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developing stories with writers and shaping drafts
rubrics_metrics.description: Developing stories with writers; working closely with the writer on each draft of their story and script, giving the writer feedback on the quality of their work, suggesting improvements that can be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical, hands-on editorial work across drafts — mentoring and concrete suggestions to improve story and script quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure scripts are suitable for production
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensuring that scripts are suitable for production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes practical considerations that affect production viability (see continuity and running time).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage practical issues: continuity and correct running time
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that practical issues, like continuity and correct running time, are adhered to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Story editors must check and enforce elements that impact shooting, scheduling, and episode length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle deadlines and late scripts (multiple writers per act)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a script is past due, multiple people may write an act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Story editors must manage schedule pressures and coordinate multiple contributors when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt to show-specific 'temperature' and etiquette
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that each show has its own temperature and its own etiquette; understand your role on that particular show and how the showrunner prefers to work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect variation in how much lower-level writers are encouraged to pitch, and whether ideas should be fully formed or just kernels — tailor your behavior to the show's culture (Marc Abrams quote).

rubrics_metrics.name: Animation: serve as head writer/oversee writers' room
rubrics_metrics.description: In American animation on productions under the jurisdiction of IATSE Local 839, the story editor is not a lower-level writer, but rather the head writer of the series who oversees the writers' room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under this model the story editor works directly with the showrunner or may even serve as showrunner; the title carries senior managerial responsibility rather than junior support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brainstorm ideas and determine the direction of the show
rubrics_metrics.description: Their role involves brainstorming ideas, determining the direction of the show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategic creative leadership: setting tonal and narrative direction beyond individual episodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct writing staff in breaking episodes and season arcs
rubrics_metrics.description: Directing the writing staff in breaking episodes and season arcs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hands-on coordination of story structure across episodes and the season; leading room sessions that decompose arcs into episode-level beats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perform rewrites on finished scripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Doing rewrites for the finished scripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Story editors are responsible for script polish and rework even after a draft is nominally complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborate with executive producers and department heads to achieve shared vision
rubrics_metrics.description: They collaborate with the executive producers and department heads to achieve a shared vision for the series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-departmental coordination to align writing with production, direction, and other departments' needs.
